blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Solomon was young when he became king, and he had asked God for one thing: an understanding heart, to judge the people well. Not long after, two women came to stand before him.

verses.text: Then came there two women, that were harlots, unto the king, and stood before him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then came there two women, that were harlots, unto the king, and stood before him.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: They lived together in the same house, and each had a baby. No one else had been there to see what happened. The first woman spoke.

verses.text: And the one woman said, O my lord, I and this woman dwell in one house; and I was delivered of a child with her in the house.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the one woman said,

segments.speaker: woman1
segments.text: O my lord, I and this woman dwell in one house; and I was delivered of a child with her in the house.

verses.text: And it came to pass the third day after that I was delivered, that this woman was delivered also: and we were together; there was no stranger with us in the house, save we two in the house.

segments.speaker: woman1
segments.text: And it came to pass the third day after that I was delivered, that this woman was delivered also: and we were together; there was no stranger with us in the house, save we two in the house.

verses.text: And this woman’s child died in the night; because she overlaid it.

segments.speaker: woman1
segments.text: And this woman’s child died in the night; because she overlaid it.

verses.text: And she arose at midnight, and took my son from beside me, while thine handmaid slept, and laid it in her bosom, and laid her dead child in my bosom.

segments.speaker: woman1
segments.text: And she arose at midnight, and took my son from beside me, while thine handmaid slept, and laid it in her bosom, and laid her dead child in my bosom.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: In the morning, she said, she woke to feed her son and found a dead child in her arms. When she looked closely, it was not her boy.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The other woman pushed back at once. No, the living child was hers. Back and forth they went, each telling the same story in reverse. There were no witnesses. It was one word against another.

verses.text: Then said the king, The one saith, This is my son that liveth, and thy son is the dead: and the other saith, Nay; but thy son is the dead, and my son is the living.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then said the king,

segments.speaker: solomon
segments.text: The one saith, This is my son that liveth, and thy son is the dead:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and the other saith,

segments.speaker: solomon
segments.text: Nay; but thy son is the dead, and my son is the living.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Any judge might have felt stuck. Instead, the king gave a startling command.

verses.text: And the king said, Bring me a sword. And they brought a sword before the king.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the king said,

segments.speaker: solomon
segments.text: Bring me a sword.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they brought a sword before the king.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The room must have gone very quiet.

verses.text: And the king said, Divide the living child in two, and give half to the one, and half to the other.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the king said,

segments.speaker: solomon
segments.text: Divide the living child in two, and give half to the one, and half to the other.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: In that moment, what was hidden came into the light.

verses.text: Then spake the woman whose the living child was unto the king, for her bowels yearned upon her son, and she said, O my lord, give her the living child, and in no wise slay it. But the other said, Let it be neither mine nor thine, but divide it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then spake the woman whose the living child was unto the king, for her bowels yearned upon her son, and she said,

segments.speaker: mother
segments.text: O my lord, give her the living child, and in no wise slay it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the other said, Let it be neither mine nor thine, but divide it.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: She would rather lose her son than see him harmed. The other woman wanted the child cut in two, so that neither of them would have him.

verses.text: Then the king answered and said, Give her the living child, and in no wise slay it: she is the mother thereof.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the king answered and said,

segments.speaker: solomon
segments.text: Give her the living child, and in no wise slay it: she is the mother thereof.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Solomon never meant to use the sword. He was looking for love, the kind that gives itself away, and it showed him the true mother.

verses.text: And all Israel heard of the judgment which the king had judged; and they feared the king: for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him, to do judgment.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And all Israel heard of the judgment which the king had judged; and they feared the king: for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him, to do judgment.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The people saw more than a clever king. They saw God's own wisdom at work in him. The story ends quietly, with a child safe in his mother's arms.

first_reader.note: First draft by the free model; Claude did the pastor and cultural read and edited it.

pastor.note: Faithful to 1 Kings 3:16-28 (and 3:9 for the request); the speech of the one woman and the true mother kept separate, as the text does not say they are the same; the women's trade (v16) is left in the stored verse, not dwelt on.

cultural.note: Both women shown as people, not types; the king's wisdom credited to God as v28.

qa.rewritten: Moderate edit: speech cuts fixed, the real mother's plea (v26) added as scripture.
